purpose: Sixth fresh generality batch. The headline work is generic Express + Prisma ORM response resolution (P1#1) and query destructuring (P1#2), verified against the official prisma-examples ORM/Express app; that app is documented separately in REMAINING-batch6.md because its two untyped JSON request bodies are intentionally left to the visible AI review rather than fabricated. The deterministic scored set below uses entirely new real codebases: two axum official examples (including raw-body extractors, a shared-state store, nested admin routers and an explicit Err(StatusCode::NOT_FOUND) arm) and a Fiber v3 recipe, proving the scanner holds across different projects and a new framework major version.

scoring.notes: Custom IntoResponse error mappings (axum-jwt AuthError) are a cross-symbol exception/error chain and are tracked separately; the scored success contracts are fully deterministic. A dedicated Express+Prisma AI-engagement sample is documented outside this gate.

projects.baseline: Official axum key-value store (5 operations): GET /{key} returns Ok(Bytes) (application/octet-stream) or Err(StatusCode::NOT_FOUND) (empty 404); POST /{key} takes an untagged bytes::Bytes raw body extractor and returns () empty 200; GET /keys returns a joined String (text/plain); DELETE /admin/keys and DELETE /admin/key/{key} come from a nested admin_routes() Router and return () empty 200.

Official axum JWT example (2 operations): POST /authorize takes Json<AuthPayload> and returns Result<Json<AuthBody>, AuthError> (200 application/json on success); GET /protected returns Result<String, AuthError> (200 text/plain). AuthError's custom IntoResponse maps to 400/401/500 and is a cross-symbol error chain tracked separately from the deterministic success contract.
Fiber v3 hello-world recipe (1 operation): app.Get("/", hello) returns a plain text string 200. Confirms Fiber v3 routing/response handling on a fresh codebase.
